title: package.json and Scripts
description: Master package.json structure, scripts, and lifecycle hooks.

data.text: The package.json file is the manifest for every JavaScript project. It defines metadata, dependencies, and scripts that automate common tasks.

rows: Start development server with hot reloading

data.text: You can run any script with npm run <script> or yarn <script>. NPM and Yarn also support shorthand aliases for common scripts like npm test and yarn test.
NPM runs lifecycle scripts automatically: preinstall, install, postinstall, prestart, poststart, etc. Yarn supports the same hooks.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Use concurrently or npm-run-all to run multiple scripts in parallel or sequence during development.

terms.definition: The package.json file describing a project.

items.question: Can I pass arguments to scripts?
items.answer: Yes. Use -- to pass arguments after the script name, e.g., npm run build -- --watch.

items.question: Are lifecycle scripts secure?
items.answer: They run arbitrary code. Review postinstall scripts from untrusted packages carefully.

items.text: Lifecycle hooks run automatically during events.
